metadata.note: The Bald Eagle Valley Railroad -- Bellefonte's real connection to the outside world, running Tyrone-Bellefonte-Lock Haven and completing the picture alongside the Bellefonte Central (see bellefonte_central.geojson), which only ever reached as far as State College. Its origins trace to the financially troubled Tyrone and Lock Haven Railroad, chartered 1857 (the Bellefonte branch itself was built before 1861); reorganized as the Bald Eagle Valley and funded directly by the Pennsylvania Railroad from 1861, it was completed through to Lock Haven in 1865. Always fully PRR-controlled and never operated independently, it was formally merged into the PRR itself in 1908. At Tyrone it met the PRR's own Middle Division main line (Altoona-Harrisburg); at Lock Haven it connected toward the Susquehanna Valley. The county's only named first-class train, the Penn-Lehigh Express (Easton-Pittsburgh via Sunbury, Williamsport, Lock Haven, Tyrone), began running in 1916 alongside PRR coach-only locals. Post-WWI highway and automobile competition eroded ridership, and the 1950 discontinuance of the remaining Altoona-Lock Haven local trains ended all scheduled passenger service in Centre County. GEOMETRY METHODOLOGY: real-traced through OpenStreetMap active/abandoned-rail data (Overpass API, shortest-path graph search); traced length 95.2 km / 59.2 mi.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Bald Eagle Valley Railroad, Bellefonte and Snowshoe Railroad), centrehistory.org (Centre County Railroads), calisphere.org (Bald Eagle Valley and Tyrone & Clearfield branches PRR timetable)
